column1: # The divergence.broiler-js fields corpus revision 5 retires: every vector Broiler.JS matches after
# milestone SJL-3.5's cut-over, under the reason scripts/conformance/number-divergences.txt gave it at
# revision 4. The reasons' text follows the table.

# legacy-octal-fraction: 07.5 is read as the one literal 7.5; 07 is a LegacyOctalIntegerLiteral, and the .5 that follows it makes the script a SyntaxError. Answered by Broiler.JS docs/roadmap/SharedLibraries.md, item SJL-14 (Broiler.JS on the shared syntax library).

# empty-exponent: A literal whose exponent has no digits (1e) evaluates to NaN instead of being a SyntaxError. Answered by Broiler.JS docs/roadmap/SharedLibraries.md, item SJL-14 (Broiler.JS on the shared syntax library).

# bigint-leading-zero: A BigInt literal with a leading zero (01n, 08n) is accepted; the grammar has no such literal, and the script is a SyntaxError. Answered by Broiler.JS docs/roadmap/SharedLibraries.md, item SJL-14 (Broiler.JS on the shared syntax library).

# bigint-fraction: A BigInt suffix after a fraction (.5n) is a TypeError when evaluated, where the n is an IdentifierStart immediately after a NumericLiteral and the script is a SyntaxError. Answered by Broiler.JS docs/roadmap/SharedLibraries.md, item SJL-14 (Broiler.JS on the shared syntax library).

# non-decimal-rounding: A hexadecimal, octal or binary integer beyond 2^53, as a literal or a string, is not converted to the nearest double with ties to even. Answered by Broiler.JS docs/roadmap/SharedLibraries.md, item SJL-3 (the number-conversion cut-over).

# long-significand-hang: StringToNumber and parseFloat do not complete for a decimal significand of more than 309 digits with a finite value: the first estimate is +Infinity and the refinement steps one unit in the last place at a time. The runner ends the evaluation at its time limit. Answered by Broiler.JS docs/roadmap/SharedLibraries.md, item SJL-3 (the number-conversion cut-over).

# long-significand-nan: StringToNumber and parseFloat give NaN for a decimal significand of more than 309 digits with a finite value and an exponent below -308: the estimate divides +Infinity by +Infinity. Answered by Broiler.JS docs/roadmap/SharedLibraries.md, item SJL-3 (the number-conversion cut-over).

# next-line-white-space: parseInt trims U+0085 (NEXT LINE) as white space; it is neither WhiteSpace nor LineTerminator, so no digit follows and the result is NaN. Answered by Broiler.JS docs/roadmap/SharedLibraries.md, item SJL-3 (the number-conversion cut-over).

# precision-argument: Number.prototype.toPrecision refuses a precision of 100.5, which ToIntegerOrInfinity makes 100, with a RangeError. Answered by Broiler.JS docs/roadmap/SharedLibraries.md, item SJL-3 (the number-conversion cut-over).

# radix-argument: Number.prototype.toString takes a radix whose ToIntegerOrInfinity is 0 (0, null, -0) as radix 10, and a NaN radix escapes as a host ArgumentException, where each is a RangeError. Answered by Broiler.JS docs/roadmap/SharedLibraries.md, item SJL-3 (the number-conversion cut-over).

# radix-64-bit: Number::toString at a radix other than 10 gives a wrong value for a magnitude of 2^63 or more: the integer part is converted through a 64-bit integer. Answered by Broiler.JS docs/roadmap/SharedLibraries.md, item SJL-3 (the number-conversion cut-over).

# radix-longer: Number::toString at a radix other than 10 gives more digits than the shortest that round-trip: the fraction is expanded digit by digit (up to 1,100 digits) instead of stopping at the shortest. Answered by Broiler.JS docs/roadmap/SharedLibraries.md, item SJL-3 (the number-conversion cut-over).

# radix-inexact: Number::toString at a radix other than 10 gives digits that do not denote the value: the fraction is expanded in double arithmetic, whose rounding error enters the digits. Answered by Broiler.JS docs/roadmap/SharedLibraries.md, item SJL-3 (the number-conversion cut-over).
